citation.authors: Hamler TC, Nguyen AW, Keith V, Qin W et al

cited_by.title: Colourism, skin tone and mental health

record.population: 837 African Americans aged 55 or over, National Survey of American Life
record.design: Cross-sectional survey with regression; skin tone self-reported
record.finding: Discrimination was linked to worse self-rated mental health and serious psychological distress, and the link with distress was stronger in darker-skinned respondents than lighter ones. For self-rated mental health the skin tone effect held for men but not women.
record.note: Older adults only; association; mechanisms not tested.
